models_evaluated: auditory large language model (voice-based assessment card and malignancy alert)

links.outcome: Reader accuracy with versus without AI assessment card; overreliance assessed via model-correctness dependence
links.effect: Accuracy 49.8% before vs 56.8% after review (diff 7.0 points; 95% CI 1.7 to 13.5); rose 14.7 points when model correct, fell 8.7 when incorrect.
links.quote: Across 800 paired assessments, reader accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after review (difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed from incorrect to correct and 43 from correct to incorrect (ratio, 2.30; 95% CI, 1.22 to 5.31).

links.outcome: Whether readers detect incorrect AI outputs (accuracy change by model correctness)
links.effect: Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect; gains depended on model correctness without clearly selective adoption.
links.quote: Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with versus without AI vs standalone model metrics
links.effect: Clinician sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions rose from 53.9% to 75.0% after AI-assisted review (difference 21.1 points; 95% CI 4.3 to 42.0).
links.quote: Sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions increased from 53.9% to 75.0% after AI-assisted review (difference, 21.1 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.3 to 42.0).

links.outcome: Model performance in held-out test set versus later temporal cohort
links.effect: Provisional-category accuracy was 72% in held-out testing and 67% in temporal validation; malignancy alert flagged 85.7% and 86.8% of lesions.
links.quote: Provisional-category accuracy was 72% in held-out testing and 67% in temporal validation.

links.outcome: Reader categorization accuracy with versus without AI
links.effect: Accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after AI review; difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5.
links.quote: Across 800 paired assessments, reader accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after review (difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed from incorrect to correct and 43 from correct to incorrect (ratio, 2.30; 95% CI, 1.22 to 5.31).

links.outcome: Clinician performance using intended AI card workflow
links.effect: Reader accuracy increased from 49.8% before to 56.8% after review; P < 0.001.
links.quote: Across 800 paired assessments, reader accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after review (difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed from incorrect to correct and 43 from correct to incorrect (ratio, 2.30; 95% CI, 1.22 to 5.31).

links.outcome: Effect of incorrect AI outputs on readers
links.effect: Accuracy rose 14.7 points when model correct, but fell 8.7 points when model incorrect.
links.quote: Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect.

links.outcome: reader accuracy change when AI model was incorrect
links.effect: Accuracy fell 8.7 points when the model was incorrect (and rose 14.7 points when correct; 43 categories changed from correct to incorrect).
links.quote: Accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect.
